questions.prompt: Trace a multi-seller checkout in MarketForge from the checkout stepper to the success screen. What happens inside the transaction, and why is it one transaction?

keyPoints.text: The checkout UI collects address, per-seller shipping, payment and an optional discount code, then posts to the checkout API.
keyPoints.quote: collects address, shipping-per-seller, payment, discount code

keyPoints.text: The route delegates to the checkout domain function, which runs inside runInTransaction.
keyPoints.quote: runs inside `runInTransaction()`

keyPoints.text: Active cart items are grouped by seller with reduce.
keyPoints.quote: groups by seller with `.reduce()`

keyPoints.text: One order is created for each seller in the cart.
keyPoints.quote: creates one order per seller

keyPoints.text: Inventory is decremented with a conditional update so concurrent buyers cannot oversell.
keyPoints.quote: decrements inventory with conditional update to avoid oversell race

keyPoints.text: Order history, transactions, payouts and notifications are written, and active cart items are cleared.
keyPoints.quote: writes order history, transactions, payouts, notifications

keyPoints.text: The transaction boundary means all checkout writes succeed or fail together, protecting money and inventory.
keyPoints.quote: all checkout writes either succeed together or fail together

questions.prompt: How is MarketForge's code organized between routes, components and src/lib, and which design patterns does that layout support?

keyPoints.text: Next.js App Router keeps React pages and API handlers in one codebase so the full request flow is visible.
keyPoints.quote: lets this project keep React pages and backend API handlers in one codebase

keyPoints.text: API routes act as thin transport adapters that push business rules into src/lib.
keyPoints.quote: route parses HTTP input/output, but pushes business rules into

keyPoints.text: Each domain module owns one business area such as orders, cart or catalog.
keyPoints.quote: each module owns a business area

keyPoints.text: Centralizing business logic keeps API handlers thin.
keyPoints.quote: centralizes business logic so API handlers stay thin

keyPoints.text: Client components hold interaction and state so page wrappers stay thin.
keyPoints.quote: keeps page wrappers thin and moves interaction/state logic into reusable components

keyPoints.text: Raw rows are shaped into UI-ready structures with filter/map/reduce/sort pipelines.
keyPoints.quote: transform raw rows into UI-ready structures step-by-step

keyPoints.text: Role checks gate admin and seller routes through requireUser.
keyPoints.quote: route access depends on user role

questions.prompt: Explain the persistence and identity choices - node:sqlite, prepared statements and cookie sessions - and the limits the guide admits.

keyPoints.text: SQLite needs no external database service but still teaches SQL, transactions and modeling.
keyPoints.quote: zero external DB service needed for local learning, but still teaches SQL, transactions, and data modeling

keyPoints.text: node:sqlite is experimental in Node 22, which is why warnings appear.
keyPoints.quote: is experimental in Node 22, so you see warnings

keyPoints.text: Direct SQL makes the mapping from app logic to database logic explicit.
keyPoints.quote: direct SQL makes data transformations explicit

keyPoints.text: Cookie sessions carry both login identity and a persistent anonymous cart.
keyPoints.quote: login identity + persistent anonymous cart sessions

keyPoints.text: The cookie model shows request-scoped identity concretely.
keyPoints.quote: clearly shows request-scoped identity

keyPoints.text: Skipping Prisma, Postgres and Stripe is simpler but not enterprise infrastructure.
keyPoints.quote: which is simpler for fundamentals but not full enterprise infra
